title: ～ば～のに (〜ba 〜noni)
longExplanation: The ～ば～のに grammar point is used to express regret or dissatisfaction about a situation that didn't happen or to express a contrary view of the actual situation. It can be translated as 'if only' or 'wish' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
formation: Verb-ば form + ～のに, い-Adjective-ば form + ～のに, な-Adjective + であれば + ～のに, Noun + であれば + ～のに

examples.jp: もっと早く来れば、電車に間に合ったのに。
examples.romaji: Motto hayaku kureba, densha ni maniatta noni.
examples.en: If only I had come earlier, I would have made it to the train.

examples.jp: もっと勉強すれば、試験に合格したのに。
examples.romaji: Motto benkyou sureba, shiken ni goukaku shita noni.
examples.en: I wish I had studied more, I would have passed the exam.

examples.jp: 彼女がもっと優しければ、彼と上手くいくのに。
examples.romaji: Kanojo ga motto yasashikereba, kare to umaku iku noni.
examples.en: If only she were kinder, she would get along with him.

examples.jp: 日本語が上手であれば、この本が読めるのに。
examples.romaji: Nihongo ga jouzu de areba, kono hon ga yomeru noni.
examples.en: I wish I were good at Japanese, then I could read this book.

usageNote: Regretful - "if only X, (but reality is otherwise)".
